label: post-deadline v2 (Nov 18)
trained_on: char n-gram model; UCI train + scams <= 2021 + real India legit SMS (train brand groups)
input: raw text; the pipeline applies scam_drift.normalise() first

tiers.RED: Likely scam - do not tap, do not reply = model flags AND the text has a link or phone number
tiers.YELLOW: Ask family before replying = model flags with no link/phone, OR a rule fires (asks for a code/PIN/password; 'hi mum / new number / wrong number' opener)
tiers.GREEN: No warning signs found = otherwise; never worded as 'safe'

rule_regex.family_opener: ^\W*(?:hi|hello|hey|hiya)?\W*(?:mum|mom|mam|mummy|mommy|dad|daddy)\b|\b(?:my new number|this is my new number|new phone number|lost my phone|broke my phone|(?:my )?phone (?:is )?broken|dropped my phone|changed my number|wrong number)\b

not_built: the 'unknown sender' condition (no sender metadata); on-device translation (non-English texts were scored on the dataset's English translation as an oracle reference)

selection.rule: lowest validation expected cost per message = 5 x 0.05 x (1 - recall) + 1 x 0.95 x false-alarm rate (5% scam rate ASSUMED; cost ratio 5:1 as in v1)
selection.selection_training: UCI train + English scams 2015-2020 (+ India train group half A1) (+ synthetic train half)
selection.validation: English scams dated 2021 (recall) + India train group half A2 (false alarms); no 2022+ data, no MOZ, no India test groups
selection.comparison_rows: fa_budget_10pct_on_india_a1 (threshold set on India A1 scores for models not trained on India) and the two link rules are scored for comparison only; the shipped choice is made among cost_5to1_oof and fa_budget_10pct_oof rows

disclaimer: This project is a prototype and is not financial advice.
